title: A physiological subpulmonary ventricle for single-ventricle heart disease

concept.text: The innovation would supply the pumping chamber missing from a Fontan circulation. In children with a functional single ventricle, staged surgery can route systemic venous blood directly to the lungs while the existing ventricle pumps blood to the body. Without a subpulmonary ventricle, blood flow through the lungs depends on elevated venous pressure. A constructed ventricle or actively contracting conduit would add mechanical work between the veins and pulmonary arteries, helping move blood through the lungs without requiring the veins to provide all the driving pressure.

The defining capability is a durable pump that fits pediatric anatomy, supplies appropriate pressure and forward flow, and accommodates years of growth without clinically significant thrombosis, obstruction, or failure. Living muscle and an equivalent mechanical pump are alternative implementations of this capability. A physiological design target discussed in the supplied research is pulsatile pulmonary systolic pressure of about 20–30 mmHg. Required stroke volume depends on how much venous return the device receives: a conduit handling only inferior vena caval flow cannot be treated as pumping the entire volume normally handled by a right ventricle. Valves and pacing can support operation, but neither they nor a passive tube independently provide the missing contractile work.

significance.text: Fontan surgery has made long-term survival possible for many people born with single-ventricle anatomy, but its circulation retains a fundamental physiological burden. Chronic venous hypertension and constrained augmentation of cardiac output contribute to a clinical picture that can include liver disease, lymphatic complications, arrhythmias, and circulatory failure. These are risks and possible outcomes, rather than an inevitable sequence for every survivor. A safe, durable subpulmonary pump could transform care by addressing the missing source of mechanical work underlying passive pulmonary flow.

The most direct potential benefits are reduced venous congestion and improved pulmonary flow and cardiac output. Normal venous pressures, normal output reserve during exercise, and stabilization of established organ disease would each require separate demonstration. Pressure generation alone does not guarantee these outcomes. In the supplied computational study, an inferior vena cava conduit improved hepatic venous pressure and output while increasing superior vena caval pressure. The clinical review also identifies several contributors to impaired exercise capacity, including chronotropic incompetence, arrhythmias, lung disease, skeletal muscle dysfunction, and deconditioning. Restoring pumping work would therefore address an important limitation without necessarily correcting every determinant of functional capacity.

Synthesis: if the pump also accommodated growth and retained its benefit over decades, it could reduce lifelong dependence on passive Fontan physiology. Constructing a whole transplantable heart would remain a further advance requiring capabilities beyond a subpulmonary pump. Creating a missing ventricle before birth shares the physiological objective, but would require a distinct developmental intervention and delivery pathway; success with a postnatal conduit would not establish that prenatal capability.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is sustained, appropriately regulated subpulmonary pumping in a growing child. The device must convert low-pressure venous inflow into useful pulmonary pressure and forward flow while remaining compatible with the available anatomy and the circulation it serves. Producing a pressure pulse in the laboratory is only one component: sufficient stroke volume, effective ejection, and net mechanical work must accompany it. For an inferior vena cava-only design, performance must be evaluated against that pathway’s inflow and its effects on the rest of the Fontan circuit.

For a living conduit, the engineering gap includes achieving much stronger coordinated contraction than the low pressures summarized in the supplied article, maintaining a blood-contacting surface that resists thrombosis, and preserving function as cardiovascular dimensions and demands change throughout childhood. The article identifies anatomical constraints, mechanical failure concerns, and endothelial cells as relevant to preventing thrombus. These are requirements for translation, not demonstrated long-term properties of an implant. An equivalent mechanical implementation would still have to satisfy the defining requirements for pediatric fit, blood compatibility, durability, and growth accommodation.

A further barrier is controlling the entire circulation rather than optimizing one local measurement. The supplied model’s opposing effects on hepatic and superior vena caval pressures show why a pump that benefits one venous territory could worsen another. Appropriate pressure must be interpreted alongside flow, filling conditions, and pulmonary vascular resistance. Successful integration must avoid exchanging one source of congestion for another, and clinical benefit must be assessed against the multiple cardiac and extracardiac causes of Fontan morbidity.

current_state.text: Grewal and colleagues’ 2026 JACC: Advances review, Contemporary Management and Future Directions of Adults Living With a Fontan Circulation, reports that 30-year survival after Fontan approaches 90%, while circulatory failure and multiorgan complications remain major concerns. This documents the substantial achievement of surgical palliation and its continuing physiological limitations. The survival figure is the review’s summary; it should not be read as a universal prognosis for every patient or surgical era.

Emuna, Hu, Marsden, and Humphrey’s 2026 npj Regenerative Medicine article summarizes previously reported tissue-engineered pulsatile conduits as generating maximum pressures of 0.1–0.8 mmHg. It compares that range with approximately 25 mmHg from a healthy right ventricle and discusses pulmonary systolic pressures of 20–30 mmHg as an ideal design target. These quantities establish the scale of the gap described by that article. The experimental range is a historical literature summary, not a verified maximum across the entire field through November 2026, and the physiological target is not an achieved implant result.

The Emuna article’s own work is theoretical and computational. In its patient-specific inferior vena cava conduit simulation, hepatic venous pressure and output improved, but superior vena caval pressure rose from 18.5 to 21.9 mmHg, reported as an 18% increase. This is evidence of a modeled design tradeoff, not a clinical observation. It supports investigating active conduits while demonstrating that useful local pumping does not automatically restore globally normal venous pressures. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate a functioning, durable implanted subpulmonary ventricle.

Unverified research-note claims: the earlier notes attribute an incidence of 2.8 surgically treated univentricular-heart cases per 10,000 live births to a 2024 Swedish study by Dalén and colleagues, DOI 10.1161/JAHA.123.031722. They also attribute stimulated luminal pressure of 1.87 mmHg in a bench conduit to Luo, Qyang, and colleagues in Acta Biomaterialia, DOI 10.1016/j.actbio.2025.06.055, with a February 2026 publication date. Neither source text is supplied, so these numbers, their measurement context, and the publication chronology cannot be verified here. The Swedish estimate concerns surgical cases and should not be generalized to all congenital single-ventricle disease. If confirmed, the attributed bench result would document a limited experimental advance, without establishing durable physiological pumping. The absence of supplied evidence does not show that either result is false.

The supplied review reports access to the full JACC article through retained XML and to the complete 17-page main Emuna article through extracted PDF text. Its conclusions do not include separate supplementary material or inspection of figures beyond the supplied extracted text. The exact 15 January 2026 publication date previously assigned to the Emuna article was not established by that text. The supplied search record is empty, so these dated sources cannot establish an exhaustive account of the field through 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed preclinical demonstration: implant the pump in a large-animal Fontan model and show sustained, physiologically appropriate pulmonary pressure and forward flow, reduced venous pressures across both caval pathways, and increased cardiac output over a prespecified period that includes somatic growth. Measure stroke volume against the venous return actually routed through the device. Pulmonary systolic pressure around 20–30 mmHg is a source-grounded physiological target, but should be interpreted alongside flow, filling pressures, and pulmonary vascular resistance. A laboratory pressure of only a few millimeters of mercury would not satisfy this proposal for restoration of physiological pumping, although it could represent useful intermediate progress. Extensive animal studies before human translation are consistent with the supplied article; this exact protocol is a proposal rather than an established standard.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained physiological pulmonary pumping lowers caval pressures and raises output

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety and reproducibility requirements: define follow-up duration and acceptable limits for thrombosis, obstruction, mechanical failure, and deterioration of either caval pathway before testing. Demonstrate continued function during growth and changing circulatory demand, rather than relying on a single favorable resting measurement. Independent replication and transparent reporting of anatomy, pump configuration, operating conditions, failures, and adverse effects would make the result convincing. Testing should establish the breadth of anatomy, size, and physiological conditions demonstrated; finite experiments cannot establish universal suitability.
completion_criteria.label: Replicated pump function during growth meets prespecified safety limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: a cohort of Fontan patients would retain hemodynamic benefit for years, with prespecified evidence that Fontan-associated liver and lymphatic disease stops progressing. Functional capacity, arrhythmia burden, adverse events, and the need for additional interventions should also be followed to determine the practical extent of benefit. Disease stabilization is an ambitious endpoint to test, not an expected consequence already established by the sources. The study should define patient selection and distinguish improvement in congestion from reversal of established tissue injury. These are proposed completion criteria, not consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Years-long hemodynamic benefit accompanies stabilized Fontan-associated liver and lymphatic disease

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PED-01, Physiological extrauterine support through fetal organ maturity, overlaps in supporting immature organs while a child develops, but concerns maintaining fetal physiology outside the uterus. PED-07 concerns supplying missing cardiac pumping work, potentially for years. PED-06, Prenatal correction that lets severe monogenic disease develop normally, overlaps with the possibility of intervention before birth; its defining objective is correction of severe monogenic disease. Prenatal creation of a ventricle is a distinct possible route toward PED-07’s physiological objective and is not demonstrated by either roster title.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-08, Restoration of nephron endowment after the nephrogenic clock stops, shares the ambition of restoring an organ capability that is absent or insufficient. Its central challenge is generating functional nephron endowment, whereas PED-07 requires a growth-compatible source of circulatory work. PED-12, Drug-free donor-specific tolerance for pediatric solid-organ grafts, could be relevant if an implementation involved donor tissue or transplantation, but immune tolerance and functional pump construction are separate capabilities. Constructing an entire transplantable heart would extend beyond this concept’s subpulmonary function.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-03, Reversal of established childhood stunting and its cognitive cost; PED-04, Controlled reopening of developmental critical periods; and PED-09, Post-symptomatic restoration of severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders, share the broader concern of recovering function after development or disease has created lasting limitations. They do not supply the missing cardiac work addressed here. PED-05, Prevention of cerebral palsy after perinatal brain injury, and PED-11, One-time in vivo correction of severe newborn metabolic disease before irreversible injury, emphasize preventing downstream injury. PED-07 likewise seeks to reduce secondary organ damage, but improvement of its circulation would not itself establish reversal of established liver, lymphatic, or other injury.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-02, Protective adaptive immunity generated by the newborn; PED-10, Function-sparing cure of H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma; and PED-13, Drug-free reset of severe pediatric autoimmune disease, address immune protection, cancer eradication, and immune disease reset respectively. Their common ground with PED-07 is durable pediatric benefit while preserving function. Their defining mechanisms and demonstrations remain distinct, and none should be merged with the subpulmonary-pump capability.

change_log.change: Preserved PED-07’s identity and integrated living and mechanical pumps as alternative implementations of the same missing capability.
change_log.reason: The concept is defined by durable restoration of subpulmonary work rather than one fabrication method.

change_log.change: Replaced guaranteed normalization of venous pressure and cardiac-output reserve with conditional benefits and independently testable outcomes.
change_log.reason: The supplied simulation worsened superior vena caval pressure, and the clinical review identifies several independent contributors to impaired exercise capacity.

change_log.change: Qualified stroke-volume requirements for an inferior vena cava-only conduit and added whole-circulation evaluation.
change_log.reason: The modeled conduit receives only part of total venous return; local improvement can coexist with deterioration elsewhere.

change_log.change: Separated historical experimental pressures, physiological design targets, and computational results.
change_log.reason: The reported 0.1–0.8 mmHg range summarizes reviewed experiments, approximately 25 mmHg is a healthy-right-ventricle comparison, and 20–30 mmHg is a design target rather than an implanted achievement.

change_log.change: Added the modeled superior vena caval pressure increase from 18.5 to 21.9 mmHg and identified it explicitly as simulation evidence.
change_log.reason: This quantitative tradeoff materially limits claims of automatic restoration of normal physiology.

change_log.change: Resolved the JACC author attribution to Grewal and colleagues and retained the review’s near-90% 30-year survival summary with scope qualifications.
change_log.reason: The validated review identifies the authors and full article, while the aggregate survival statement does not establish every patient’s prognosis.

change_log.change: Retained the Swedish incidence and attributed Luo bench-pressure result as explicitly unverified research-note claims.
change_log.reason: Their source texts are absent. Qualification preserves potentially useful information without treating it as established or interpreting missing evidence as disproof.

change_log.change: Removed reliance on an exact January publication date and an asserted later-result chronology.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish those temporal details.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include both caval pathways, safety, growth, independent replication, and defined practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: Pressure generation alone cannot establish durable clinical benefit, and finite demonstrations establish tested breadth rather than universal applicability.

change_log.change: Preserved the supplied review’s extraction limits and lack of an exhaustive freshness search.
change_log.reason: Full main-article text does not substitute for unexamined supplements or figures, and dated evidence cannot establish the complete field as of November 2026.

change_log.change: Clarified prenatal ventricular creation and whole-heart construction, and mapped relevant distinctions across the supplied roster.
change_log.reason: Shared physiological objectives do not make developmental intervention, whole-organ construction, immune tolerance, and pump engineering interchangeable.

unresolved_issues: The Swedish incidence estimate of 2.8 surgical cases per 10,000 live births remains unverified from the supplied material, including its population definition and applicability beyond the studied setting.

The attributed Luo result of 1.87 mmHg requires source verification, including measurement conditions, comparability with earlier conduit pressures, publication date, and chronology. The review’s recommendation to remove it and the Swedish estimate was not adopted literally; both were retained as explicitly unverified claims to preserve the supplied research without inventing confirmation.
The exact publication date of the Emuna article is not established by the supplied extracted text.
No supplied evidence establishes durable implanted performance during growth or multiyear human benefit.
The design changes needed to improve both caval pathways without introducing other hemodynamic costs remain unresolved.
Whether restoring subpulmonary work can stabilize or reverse established liver and lymphatic disease remains a clinical question.
Specific follow-up durations, safety limits, patient-selection criteria, and acceptable intervention burdens for a convincing demonstration remain to be defined.
The empty supplied search record prevents an exhaustive assessment through 1 November 2026; separate supplements and figures were not assessed beyond the review’s stated extraction scope.
